title: documation fix for django 1.7 "App registry isn't ready yet"
body:
The celery app file needs to call django.setup in django 1.7 or you get an exception stating "App registry isn't ready yet" when a task is run.

See https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/1.7/#standalone-scripts

The documentation for first steps with django (http://docs.celeryproject.org/en/master/django/first-steps-with-django.html) need to be updated to reflect this.

title: Celery 3.1.13 is not respecting updates to BROKER_URL
body:
Up to Celery 3.1.12 I was able to define a config file named foo with contents like:

```
BROKER_URL = "amqp://guest:guest@localhost:5671//"
bar_BROKER_URL = "amqp://guest@localhost:5672/"
```

Which would be used in the following manner:

```
app = Celery('x')
app.config_from_object(foo)
app.conf.BROKER_URL = foo.bar_BROKER_URL
```

Now in Celery 3.1.13 this bar_BROKER_URL is not respected anymore, celery really wants to connect to the port 5671 even though I'm telling it to explicitly not use it. Was this intentional?

title: Celery worker stops responding after running the same task for 4th time.
Chord for a group with retries invokes callback before group finishes
body:
Celery : *_3.1.16 *_

**Given**: Chord with group tasks(a, b) and call back  c
chord ( group(a,b), c)

**And**: Task a, b are retryable (They retry on exception)

**When**: I call chord ,  the callback task c gets invoked  and  a throws exception and retries.

**Then**: Chord does not wait for results for the retry and calls the callback even before task "a" could finish.

Ideally I would expect callback to be called when a,b finish the retry logic and are successful.

title: Chord callback is executed while tasks are in retry state
body:
The code looks like:

```
chunk_tasks = []
for index, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
    chunk_tasks.append(
                import_chunk.s(meta.pk, chunk, start_row, has_labels=has_labels)
            )
g = group(chunk_tasks)
chord(g)(import_completed.s(meta.pk))
```

However some of the import chunk tasks can fail and be retried several times. The problem is that the import_completed which should be called after all tasks are completed is called while some of the tasks in the group are still in the retry state.
Is this a bug or I have missed setting up something?

title: Is there way to specify expiry when creating a celery task?
body:
Specifically I use `shared_task` decorator to create a celery task.
I tried the obvious `@shared_task(expires=3)` but it doesn't seem to work.

Is there a way to tell this task is supposed to expire *\* seconds after it is received as you can do with `apply_async` in calling time?

I tried to see what @shared_decorator does by looking at the code, but it wasn't obvious... 

(I copied the question from SO, cause it didn't get enough attention. http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32217358/is-there-way-to-specify-expiry-when-creating-a-celery-task)

Hello,

After upgrading to celery 4.1.1 + kombu 4.2, when launching celery multi with --workdir (which launches celery worker with --detach and --workdir), the workers start and then immediately stop with no log (even in debug mode) and only the log of the master process is generated.

This issue appeared in 4.1.1, 4.1.0 is not affected

Thanks

title: Docs seem to suggest that ignore_result can be set on `delay`
body:
# Checklist
- [x] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22+)
  for similar or identical bug reports.
- [x] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22)
  for existing proposed fixes.
- [x] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/master)
  to find out if the bug was already fixed in the master branch.
- [x] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues in this issue
      (If there are none, check this box anyway).

## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates

#### Related Issues

- introduced by: PR #4745

#### Possible Duplicates

- None

# Description
The [user guide for tasks](https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/7f9daab9d3007d2a52f7813cf12dd7fa5666c98b/docs/userguide/tasks.rst#tips-and-best-practices) states:  "Results can be enabled/disabled on a per-execution basis, by passing the `ignore_result` boolean parameter, when calling `apply_async` _or `delay`_" (emphasis mine)

To me, this seems to suggest that you could so something like `mytask.delay(ignore_result=True)`. However, that will just cause the kwarg to be passed through to the task itself, or rather, it causes an exception:

    TypeError: mytask() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ignore_result'

Looking at the [user guide on calling tasks](https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/7f9daab9d3007d2a52f7813cf12dd7fa5666c98b/docs/userguide/calling.rst#basics), it becomes clear that `delay` is just a "Shortcut to send a task message, _but doesn’t support execution options_" (emphasis mine) and hence `apply_async` must be used instead.

# Suggestions
Unless I'm completely misunderstanding something here, I suggest that it is made more clear in the user guide for tasks that usage of `apply_async` rather than `delay` is required to use the `ignore_result` kwarg.

title: Beat fires tasks on start
body: I am using CeleryBeat for cron jobs. Sometimes when I start celery the tasks will fire on startup even tho its not the time I scheduled for them to fire. I cannot find any info on this issue anywhere, other than for RedBeat, which im not using. https://github.com/sibson/redbeat/issues/79

title: `_revoke()` does not pass `Request` to `mark_as_revoked()`, preventing chord bookkeeping
body:
## Description

When a task that belongs to a chord is revoked through the worker control command (`app.control.revoke(task_id)`), the task is correctly marked as `REVOKED` in the backend, but the chord bookkeeping is not updated when the task is already known by the worker.

The issue is in `celery/worker/control.py`, where `_revoke()` calls:

```python
state.app.backend.mark_as_revoked(
    task_id, reason='revoked', store_result=True
)
```

without passing the task's `Request`.

However, `BaseBackend.mark_as_revoked()` performs chord bookkeeping only when a `request` is provided:

```python
if request and request.chord:
    self.on_chord_part_return(request, state, exc)
```

This creates an inconsistency with the normal worker-side revocation path, which passes the request to `mark_as_revoked()`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a chord with multiple tasks.
2. Ensure a chord member has already been received by a worker so its `Request` is locally known.
3. Revoke that task using the worker control API:

```python
app.control.revoke(task_id)
```

4. Check the backend state of the revoked task.
5. Observe the chord completion behavior.

The revoked task is stored as `REVOKED`, but `on_chord_part_return()` is not called for that chord member.

## Expected behavior

Revoking a chord member should update the chord bookkeeping in the same way as normal worker-side revocation, so that the chord can account for the revoked member and continue according to the configured chord behavior.

## Actual behavior

The task is marked as `REVOKED`, but because `_revoke()` does not pass the locally-known `Request`, `BaseBackend.mark_as_revoked()` cannot detect that the task belongs to a chord.

As a result, `on_chord_part_return()` is not called and the chord may remain waiting for that member.

## Root cause

The control-command revocation path does not propagate the existing `Request` object to the backend.

The normal request-based revocation path already does this:

```python
self.task.backend.mark_as_revoked(
    self.id,
    reason,
    request=self._context,
    store_result=self.store_errors,
)
```

but `_revoke()` does not.

## Proposed fix

Reuse the existing `_find_requests_by_id()` helper in `celery/worker/control.py` to associate locally-known task IDs with their `Request` objects, and pass the request to `mark_as_revoked()`:

```python
requests_by_id = {
    request.id: request
    for request in _find_requests_by_id(task_ids)
}

for task_id in task_ids:
    state.app.backend.mark_as_revoked(
        task_id,
        reason='revoked',
        store_result=True,
        request=requests_by_id.get(task_id),
    )
```

A regression test should verify that when a locally-known chord task is revoked through `_revoke()`, its `Request` is passed to `mark_as_revoked()` and chord bookkeeping is triggered.

## Scope / limitation

This addresses the case where the revoked task has already been received by a worker and its `Request` is locally available.

If a task has never been consumed by any worker, there may be no local `Request` from which to obtain the chord metadata. That is a separate issue and is not addressed by this proposed change.

## Additional context

This behavior appears to be related to the change that made control-command revocation immediately update the backend state to `REVOKED`. The backend status update works correctly, but the corresponding chord side effect is currently skipped because the `Request` is not propagated.

title: no-value-for-parameter false positive with sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid.hybrid_method
body:
### Bug description


Taking an example from the [`sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid.hybrid_method` docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/hybrid.html#sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid.hybrid_method):

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid import hybrid_method
from sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid import hybrid_property
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from sqlalchemy.orm import mapped_column


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class Interval(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'interval'

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    start: Mapped[int]
    end: Mapped[int]

    def __init__(self, start: int, end: int):
        self.start = start
        self.end = end

    @hybrid_property
    def length(self) -> int:
        return self.end - self.start

Interval.length() # <--- false positive here
```

`Interval.length` is both a class method and an instance method, and can be called as a class method when building SQL queries. pylint reports no-value-for-parameter on this usage.


### Configuration

_No response_

### Command used

```shell
pylint foo.py
```


### Pylint output

```python
E1120: No value for argument 'self' in unbound method call (no-value-for-parameter)
```

No error.

title: False positive when using "/" for positional arguments (too-many-positional-arguments)
body:
### Bug description
R0917: Too many positional arguments (7/5) (too-many-positional-arguments)
Pylint has trouble detecting positional arguments when using "/". In there, only a, b and c are positional while d, e and f are keyword parameters.

This behavior did not happen with pylint 3.0.3, astroid 3.0.3

```python
class Foo:
    def __init__(self, a, b, c, /, d=None, e=None, f=None):
        pass
```

```python
"""Cameras and images
===================

This demo shows with the example of the ``DummyGrabber``
how you acquire an image and apply some filters."""

from itom import dataIO
from itom import dataObject

# Initialize a ``DummyGrabber`` camera

cam.setParam("bpp", 8)
# start camera (only once)
cam.startDevice()

# show live image of camera
liveImage(cam)

###############################################################################
# .. hint:: The live images tries to acquire and get up to 50 images per second
#     from the camera. If you want to acquire images by yourself in a script, you need
#     to stop the timer of the live images for a certain amount of time. After you are
#     done with your manual acquisition, you can restart the timer again.

currentStatus = cam.getAutoGrabbing()
print("Current value of auto grabbing property of the camera:", currentStatus)

cam.setAutoGrabbing(False)

###############################################################################

result = []
d = dataObject()  # empty data object where the image should be put in

    cam.getVal(d)  # d is a shallow copy of the camera image

###############################################################################

saveIDC("image1.idc", {"result": result, "description": "sample 1"})

###############################################################################

result2 = loaded_objects["result"]

# plot the 3rd image from the list

sizex = cam.getParam("sizex")
sizey = cam.getParam("sizey")
bpp = cam.getParam("bpp")

    d = dataObject([num, sizey, sizex], "uint8")
else:
    d = dataObject([num, sizey, sizex], "uint16")

    cam.copyVal(d[idx, :, :])  # partial deep copy into one part of the 3d object d

###############################################################################
# Calculate mean value of image stack in z-direction.
result_mean = dataObject()

algorithms.calcMeanZ(d, result_mean, ignoreInf=0, calcStd=0)
# result_mean is a 3d Object with [1 x sizey x sizex] dimensions.
# We squeeze it to get a 2D Object
result_mean = result_mean.squeeze()

result_mean.setTag("title", f"mean value of {num} acquisitions")
result_mean.axisUnits = ("px", "px")
result_mean.axisDescriptions = ("y", "x")
plot(result_mean)
###############################################################################
# .. image:: ../../_static/demoCameraAndImages_1.png
#    :width: 100%

###############################################################################
# Apply Gaussian filter onto the mean image.
result_filter = dataObject()
kernelVal = 9
algorithms.gaussianFilter(
    result_mean, result_filter, kernelx=kernelVal, kernely=kernelVal
)

###############################################################################
# Copy meta information from source ``dataObject``.
result_filter.copyMetaInfo(result_mean)
result_filter.setTag("title", f"Gaussian filter with kernel {kernelVal}")
plot(result_filter)
###############################################################################
# .. image:: ../../_static/demoCameraAndImages_2.png
#    :width: 100%

# reset the auto grabbing functionality of possibly connected live images
cam.setAutoGrabbing(currentStatus)

# end camera
cam.stopDevice()
```

title: Allow the possibility to assign None to a typed variable without raising warnings
body:
### Current problem

In compiled languages like **Java**, you can assign the **null** value to a typed variable. The compiler never complains.
```
String txt = "test";
// more code here
txt = null;
```

When doing the same thing in **Python**, the linters complain with the warning: `Expected type 'str', got 'None' instead`
```
x: str = "test"
# more code here
x = None
```
Can we have the **Python** linters stop complaining about **None** assignments ?

### Desired solution

No more warnings like `Expected type 'xxxxx', got 'None' instead`

Stop the linter raising a warning if the **None** value is assign to a type variable


### Additional context

Same thing for functions

If a functions returns a value, why the linter complains if **None** is returned ?

```
def my_function() -> str:
    if condition:
        return "test"
    else:
        return None
```
Again, with **Java** we dont have compiler complains with a similar code

```python
    a, b = object.method()
```

```python
        d = -1
```

title: Pylint skipping similarly named project directory.
body:
### Bug description

```python
In working on my project, I found that there was a discrepancy between the number of files being checked and how many files I had in my project, which includes both a `applications` and a `applications_api` module. In single stepping through `PyLinter._discover_files()`, I found that it would first walk over `applications`, add it to the `skip_subtrees` list, then when it hit the `applications_api` module, it would falsely skip it as having already been discovered.

Given that both of these are directories which include an `__init__.py` file, the solution is to append the OS directory separator to the name when appending the directory to the `skip_subtrees` list on line 688. I will be following this up with a PR with that fix.

The URL for my project is https://github.com/cinnion/job-application-tracker and I am running tests against the version tagged v1.99.1.
```

### Configuration

```ini
[tool.pylint.main]
django-settings-module="job_application_tracker.settings"
load-plugins = [
    "pylint_django",
    "pylint_per_file_ignores",
]
max-line-length = 120
ignore = [
    ".git",
    ".venv",
    "__pycache__",
    "manage.py",
    "node_modules"
]
jobs = 0
recursive = true
source-roots = "."
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint --verbose --recursive=y .

or

pylint --verbose --recursive=y $(git ls-files '*.py')
```

### Pylint output

```python
For the command `pylint --verbose --recursive=y .`, the output is as follows (less the fixmes):


(.venv) [cinnion@wing-1 job-application-tracker]$ pylint --verbose --recursive=y .
Using config file /home/cinnion/git.github/job-application-tracker/pyproject.toml

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 9.98/10 (previous run: 9.98/10, +0.00)
Checked 43 files/modules (), skipped 0 files/modules



With the command `pylint --verbose --recursive=y $(git ls-files '*.py')`, the output is as follows:


(.venv) [cinnion@wing-1 job-application-tracker]$ pylint --verbose --recursive=y $(git ls-files '*.py')
Using config file /home/cinnion/git.github/job-application-tracker/pyproject.toml

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Checked 58 files/modules (), skipped 3 files/modules
```

### Expected behavior

I would have expected more than 43 files to have been checked in the first case. In debugging, I tracked down 6 files as being "legitimately" skipped, due to an undocumented behaviour of `pylint-django` adding "migrations" to the ignore list, but that still leaves 9 files being missed, which is directly attributable to it skipping `applications_api` in the walk of the tree in `_discover_files()`. This has been verified after I added my fix for issue #10968 to the code.

title: E1121 (too-many-function-args) triggered incorrectly when metaclass __call__ accepts more arguments than class __init__
body:
### Bug description


When instantiating a class, pylint strictly checks the arguments against the class's `__init__`. However, if the class uses a metaclass that overrides `__call__` with a different signature, the metaclass's `__call__` signature should dictate the valid arguments, not `__init__`.

This results in pylint incorrectly raising E1121 on valid code.

```python
class Meta(type):
    def __call__(cls, a: int, b: int) -> "MyClass":
        return super().__call__(a)

class MyClass(metaclass=Meta):
    def __init__(self, a: int) -> None:
        self.a = a

MyClass(1, 2)
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint main.py
```

### Pylint output

```python
************* Module main                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
main2.py:12:0: E1121: Too many positional arguments for constructor call (too-many-function-args)
```

### Expected behavior

I'd expect pylint to refer to the metaclass's `__call__` instead of strictly refering to the class's `__init__`.

title: False positive: `nested-min-max` drops trailing arguments when suggesting a splat rewrite
body:
### Bug description

`nested-min-max` (W3301), when it suggests flattening a nested `min`/`max` into a splat call, silently **drops every argument positioned after the splatted one**, so the suggested code computes a different result than the original.

```python
LIST = [1, 2, 3]
max(max(LIST), 5, 7)   # suggests `max(*LIST)`     -> drops 5, 7  (evaluates to 3, not 7)
max(4, max(LIST), 7)   # suggests `max(4, *LIST)`  -> drops 7
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint --disable=all --enable=nested-min-max a.py
```

### Pylint output

```
a.py:2:0: W3301: Do not use nested call of 'max'; it's possible to do 'max(*LIST)' instead (nested-min-max)
```

### Expected behavior

The suggestion should preserve the trailing arguments, e.g. `max(max(LIST), 5, 7)` -> `max(*LIST, 5, 7)`.

### Root cause

In `pylint/checkers/nested_min_max.py`, the splat rewrite builds the new args with `*fixed_node.args[idx + 1 : idx]`. That slice has `start > stop`, so it is always empty and every argument after the splat position is discarded. It should be `fixed_node.args[idx + 1 :]`.

This is the same class of defect as #11130 / #11131 (the `key=`/`default=` drop), via a different code path — existing fixtures only splat the **last** argument, where the empty slice happens to coincide with the correct one, so the bug is untested.

### Pylint version

```
pylint 4.x (main branch), astroid 4.x
```

title: False positive undefined-variable for self-referential return annotation in a PEP 695 generic class
body:
### Bug description

Pylint reports `E0602: Undefined variable 'uniqdict'` when a method in a [PEP 695](https://peps.python.org/pep-0695/) generic class uses the enclosing class in its return annotation.

```python
"https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/11211"
class uniqdict[K, V](dict[K, V]):
    def __ior__(self, other, /) -> uniqdict[K, V]:
        return self
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint --rcfile=/dev/null --disable=all --enable=undefined-variable --py-version=3.12 pylint.py
```

### Pylint output

```python
pylint.py:3:35: E0602: Undefined variable 'uniqdict' (undefined-variable)
```

### Expected behavior

no diagnostics

### Pylint version

```shell
pylint 4.0.6
astroid 4.1.2
Python 3.14.6
```

### OS / Environment

MSYS_NT-10.0-26100

### Larger real-world example
```python
import collections.abc

class uniqdict[K, V](dict[K, V]):
    """A mapping whose existing keys cannot be assigned different values."""

    def __setitem__(self, key: K, value: V) -> None:
        try:
            if (old := super().__getitem__(key)) != value:
                raise ValueError(self.__class__.__name__, key, old, value)
        except KeyError:
            super().__setitem__(key, value)

    update = collections.abc.MutableMapping.update

    def __ior__(self, other, /) -> uniqdict[K, V]:
        self.update(other)
        return self
```

title: duplicate-code drops every copy of a block after the first two
body:
### Bug description

When the same block appears in three or more files, `duplicate-code` reports only the first pair. Every further copy is dropped silently.

`a.py`, `b.py` and `c.py` are identical:

```python
def f(a):
    x = a + 1
    y = x * 2
    z = y - 3
    w = z / 4
    return w
```

### Command used

```shell
symilar -d 4 a.py b.py c.py
```

### Pylint output

```
6 similar lines in 2 files
==a.py:[0:6]
==b.py:[0:6]
   ...
TOTAL lines=18 duplicates=6 percent=33.33
```

### Expected behavior

`6 similar lines in 3 files`, listing `c.py` as well, with `duplicates=12`.

The cause is the `break` in `Symilar._compute_sims`. When a new pair shares a chunk with an existing group, the pair is discarded instead of being added to that group. `tests/test_similar.py::test_duplicate_code_raw_strings_all` has this baked in: its docstring says "Test similar lines in 3 similar files", but it asserts `Similar lines in 2 files`.

On real code (`min-similarity-lines=6`, tests and migrations excluded), merging pairs into groups gives the following. No chunk reported today is lost.

| Corpus | Chunk locations reported today | After fix | Groups with 3+ copies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Django 5.1.2 | 254 | 322 | 44 (largest: 10 copies) |
| scikit-learn main | 118 | 135 | 13 |
| httpx 0.28.0 | 24 | 35 | 7 |
| pylint 4.1.3 | 20 | 22 | 2 |

### Pylint version

```shell
main (2fc0591)
```

title: --jobs > 1 duplicates every message emitted by a --load-plugins checker
body:
**Bug description**

```python
# demo.py
try:
    pass
except (ValueError, Exception):
    pass
```

With `--jobs` > 1, messages coming from checkers loaded through `--load-plugins` (or `init-hook`)
are emitted twice, and the score is computed from the duplicated count.

Two checker instances end up registered in the same worker process and `open()` is called twice per
file, so this is not a scheduling race: 5 runs out of 5 give the same result, with `-j2` as well as
with `-j0`.

**Configuration**

None — the plugin is passed on the command line, no rcfile is used.

**Command used**

```console
$ pylint --load-plugins=pylint.extensions.overlapping_exceptions \
    --disable=all --enable=overlapping-except --score=n -j1 demo.py
$ pylint --load-plugins=pylint.extensions.overlapping_exceptions \
    --disable=all --enable=overlapping-except --score=n -j2 demo.py
```

An extension shipped with pylint is used only to keep this report reproducible; a 10-line custom
plugin behaves the same way, so what matters is the entry point, not the checker itself.

**Pylint output** (main, `1a60ec190`)

```console
# -j1
demo.py:3:7: W0714: Overlapping exceptions (Exception is an ancestor class of ValueError) (overlapping-except)

# -j2
demo.py:3:7: W0714: Overlapping exceptions (Exception is an ancestor class of ValueError) (overlapping-except)
demo.py:3:7: W0714: Overlapping exceptions (Exception is an ancestor class of ValueError) (overlapping-except)
```

With `--score` enabled the rating drops as well (7.50/10 with `-j1`, 5.00/10 with `-j2`).

**Expected behavior**

One message per occurrence and the same score, whatever `--jobs` is.

**Pylint version**

```console
pylint 4.2.0-dev0 (main, 1a60ec190)   # also reproduced on 4.0.6
astroid 4.0.4
Python 3.12.10 (tags/v3.12.10:0cc8128, Apr  8 2025, 12:21:36) [MSC v.1943 64 bit (AMD64)]
```

**OS / Environment**

Windows 11 (`Windows-11-10.0.26100-SP0`). Nothing platform specific: it is a duplicated
registration, not a scheduling issue.

**Additional dependencies**

None.

---

## Additional context: suspected cause

Not a proposed fix, just the result of local investigation.

`_worker_initialize()` deregisters `_registered_dynamic_plugin_checkers` before calling
`load_plugin_modules(..., force=True)`, precisely so that the "old" checker does not survive the
re-registration — that is the fix from #10642. The set is filled in `config_initialization.py` as
`_registered_checkers.difference(default_checkers)`, and `default_checkers` is snapshotted *after*
`Run.__init__` already loaded the `--load-plugins` modules (and after `init-hook` ran). Those
checkers are therefore part of the baseline, never enter the set, and the deregistration is a no-op.

Measured on main (`1a60ec190`), one message expected per file:

| plugin given by | `-j1` | `-j2` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--load-plugins` | 1 | **2** |
| `init-hook` | 1 | **2** |
| `load-plugins` in rcfile | 1 | 1 |

The rcfile row is the one #10642 covers. On the 4.0 branch the rcfile path is affected as well,
since that branch predates #10642.

I have a patch for `main` with a regression test and will open a PR referring to this issue.

```
   and M depends on P (tag 4.8.0), H is forbidden.
  So, because M depends on H (tag 4.5.0), version solving failed.
```

Let's see version resolving charts:

```
  M (main)
  +--P (tag=4.8.0)
  +--H (tag=4.5.0)
     +--P (tag=4.8.0)
```

Look P is same in our cases but provided as source code and `poetry` solve as different version.

title: Allow --no-update on add
body:
<!--
    Hi there! Thank you for submitting a feature request!

    Before you submit your issue, please review and follow the instructions at
    https://python-poetry.org/docs/contributing/#suggesting-enhancements.
-->

<!-- All the below steps should be completed before submitting your issue. Checked checkbox should look like this: [x] -->
- [x] I have searched the [issues](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/issues) of this repo and believe that this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I have searched the [FAQ](https://python-poetry.org/docs/faq/) and general [documentation](https://python-poetry.org/docs/) and believe that my question is not already covered.

## Feature Request
<!-- Now feel free to write your issue, and please be as descriptive as possible! -->
Hi, and thanks for your work on Poetry.
I would love to have the flag `--no-update` available on add. As it is now, adding a new dependency often inadvertently updates a completely unrelated (recursive) dependency in the lock file. When poetry does this it is usually because the update is considered "safe", but for our setup we *really* only want to update any dependencies at certain times.
This is because we use `poetry2nix` in the background, and some updates might break the dependency build (for example when a new bcrypt version is released)

Currently we work around this by doing:
1. `poetry add --lock <dependency>`
2. Revert the lock file
3. `poetry lock --no-update`

(Don't worry about the `--lock`, this is because we don't actually want to install the dependencies in the system)

Instead, I would love to be able to go `poetry add --lock --no-update <dependency>` and be on my way

Thanks for your time :)
<!-- Thanks again 🙌 ❤ -->

title: Scripts defined in `[project.gui-scripts]` are not made available by `poetry install`
body:
### Description

https://python-poetry.org/docs/pyproject/#gui-scripts

> When a script is added or updated, run `poetry install` to make them available in the project’s virtualenv.

However, on Windows, any GUI scripts defined here are not actually made available in the `<venv>\Scripts` folder. So defining a gui-script named "mygui", running `poetry install`, and then running `mygui` from the active venv or `poetry run mygui` fails with the following output:

```
'mygui' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
```

This only affects the virtual env, as GUI scripts defined here are properly included in the built wheel's `entry_points.txt` when running `poetry build`.

Here is a very simple GUI script to go along with the pyproject.toml further down:
```python
from PySide6 import QtWidgets

def main():
    app = QtWidgets.QApplication([])
    main_window = QtWidgets.QMainWindow()
    main_window.show()
    return app.exec()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    sys.exit(main())
```

### Workarounds

Moving the script definition(s) to either of `[project.scripts]` or `[tool.poetry.scripts]` makes the scripts available. However, in doing this, they are no longer GUI scripts.
